Jana (oncall): :rotating_light: incident-bot paged for repeated ECC corrections on gpu-node-47, initial spike at ~03:07 UTC. Putting details here for handoff and tuning discussion.

incident-bot: ALERT gpu.ecc.count high on gpu-node-47 (count=12 in 5m). Severity: page

Jana (oncall): quick check — is this a noisy flapping alert or real hardware? I'm seeing node started draining briefly.

Miguel (eng-sre): I'm on it. Pulling telemetry now. Can someone confirm whether any user-facing errors were reported? @Priya

Priya (cust-succ): We got one p1 ticket from AcmeCorp complaining about failed inferences ~03:10-03:20 UTC. They said some requests timed out.

Leah (platops): Looks like kubelet started a graceful drain at 03:08 and completed at 03:12. Pod restarts for inference workers on that node were seen. Might be related to ECC burst causing driver reset.

Akash (eng-runtime): Logs show repeated nvml ECC warnings followed by transient driver resets. Model-serving load at that time was higher-than-usual (seq len spikes from a batch job). Sample metric:

```
node=gpu-node-47 gpu.ecc.corrected: 12
gpu.memory.used_pct: 87.4
gpu.temp: 83C
```

Miguel (eng-sre): Right — two issues layered: higher VRAM usage and an ECC flash. The current alert rule is pretty sensitive: `gpu.ecc.count > 3 in 5m` and triggers pages. That's noisy for medium-load corridors.

Jana (oncall): For immediate mitigation we re-scheduled batch jobs off that node and un-drained after driver stabilize. Node is back in rotation. Customer impact: short timeouts for some tenants, no data loss. Logged with incident ticket INC-2026-1842.

Leah (platops): Postmortem action: tune ECC alert to avoid paging on single transient corrected errors. Proposal:
- keep `gpu.ecc.count` as warning for >=2 in 5m
- page if `gpu.ecc.count >= 6` within 10m OR if driver-reset events > 0

Miguel (eng-sre): +1 to multi-condition page. Also add correlation with `node.drain.start` events so we don't double-page during automated drains.

Akash (eng-runtime): We should also add a dashboard panel for 'ECC burst patterns' with a small histogram and a timeline of driver resets, memory usage, and active batches. Proposal for panel queries:

```
- sum(rate(gpu_ecc_corrected_total[1m])) by (node)
- increases(driver_reset_count[5m]) by (node)
- gpu_memory_used_bytes / gpu_memory_total_bytes
```

Miguel (eng-sre): I'll create a new alert group `gpu-health-ecc-bursts` with these rules and a suppress window for automated orchestrated drains (suppress if `node.drain.active == true`).

Jana (oncall): Action items:
- Miguel: draft alert rule changes + suppression logic and run a simulated replay against last 30 days of metrics (due EOD) :memo:
- Akash: add dashboard panel and wire up driver reset metric (due +2 days) :bar_chart:
- Leah: add runbook section for 'ECC burst with driver resets' and update drain policy doc to mention suppression hooks (due +3 days) :book:
- Priya: notify customers who had timeouts with a short incident summary (hold until we have postmortem) :email:

Priya (cust-succ): I'll prepare a short note and hold for postmortem review. cc @Jana

incident-bot: NOTE: next-gen suppression API now available. See /ops/suppressions in the console.

Miguel (eng-sre): Running a quick query now to estimate how many pages this change would have suppressed historically. Early look — about 62% of ECC pages would have been warnings instead of pages over the last 90 days; mostly during sustained batch windows.

Akash (eng-runtime): Two extra considerations:
- VRAM usage threshold: we saw 87% mem used; maybe add a composite rule that escalates if ecc.count > threshold AND gpu.memory.used_pct > 80%
- Thermal correlation: temps were 82-84C but within spec. Add temp trend check to avoid conflating normal high-load heat with failing hardware.

Miguel (eng-sre): Agree. New composite page condition candidate:
`(ecc_count >=6 AND (memory_pct >=85 OR driver_resets > 0)) OR (driver_resets >=1 && ecc_count >=3)`

Jana (oncall): That looks good. Let's be careful with thresholds — keep pages for clear reliability signals, warnings for noisy corrected errors.

Leah (platops): I'll prototype the dashboard layout in Grafana and link it to the runbook. I'll include a discrete 'operator action' widget with common remediation steps (reschedule batches, cordon node, nvml dump collection).

Miguel (eng-sre): I'll open PR for alert rules with unit tests that feed synthetic metrics. Tentative PR title: `alert(gpu-health): ecc suppression + composite thresholds`

Jana (oncall): If no objections, we'll roll the rule to staging by tomorrow and monitor noise. We'll defer rollback window to 72h if noise increases.

Akash (eng-runtime): One last ask: can we annotate the time series with customer-visible incidents for easier triage? e.g., overlay INC-IDs on the dashboard. Helps correlate customer reports.

Priya (cust-succ): That will be awesome.

Miguel (eng-sre): Noted. I'll include an annotation webhook in the dashboard config.

Jana (oncall): Thanks team. Keeping this thread open for updates. Closing on-call for now, passing to Miguel for the alert PR and Akash for dashboard. :thumbsup:

--
Follow-ups will be posted here. INC-2026-1842
